title: Chat token synchronizer and onboarding resilience playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We observe intermittent mismatches between tokenizer-produced subtoken boundaries and chat template role delimiters for a subset of newly onboarded model bundles. These mismatches surface as off-by-one tokenization during pinned rollouts and cause downstream perf-profile noise, incorrect prefix caching, and (rarely) truncated structured outputs. This ticket implements a two-part solution: a lightweight "synchronizer" service that runs during onboarding to reconcile lexical/role boundaries and a resilience playbook that enables automatic detection, non-disruptive rollback, and targeted corrective transformations when mismatches are detected in production telemetry.

Goals/Acceptance criteria:
1) Synchronizer runs as part of the onboarding pipeline and flags model bundles with token-role boundary drift without requiring full model recompile; failures must be surfaced to PM/Oncall and gate the final publish step unless marked safe-for-degraded.
2) When a flagged bundle is pinned to customer traffic, the system can apply an in-flight template shim (non-invasive delimiter mapping) that preserves token counts and role semantics for the majority of use cases (>95% of template examples).
3) Produce automated regression tests (unit + integration) exercising: (a) subtoken splits across role markers, (b) prefix/KV cache alignment, (c) structured output truncation scenarios.
4) Include telemetry dashboards that surface tokenization divergence rate, cache hit degradation, and rollback triggers; these dashboards must be linked from the rollout UI.

Approach and design choices:
- Synchronizer design: a transient, language-agnostic probe that generates a representative set of prompt envelopes (system/user/assistant role permutations + edge punctuation/unicode cases) and compares tokenizer boundaries against Redwood canonical chat template parser. The probe emits a compact divergence vector (per-template) and a suggested minimal mapping (e.g., escape/unescape tokens, delimiter re-anchoring). The probe intentionally avoids modifying model bundles; it produces a mapping artifact that the onboarding pipeline can optionally apply as a shim.
- Shim strategy: prefer a runtime shim applied at the SDK/ingress layer for Hosted/Dedicated, and as a pre-load transformation for Private deployments. Shim implementation focuses on syntactic adjustments (role marker normalizers, narrow whitespace coalescing) rather than semantic rewrites to minimize risk.
- Rollout/resilience playbook: when divergence exceeds thresholds in prod telemetry, the rollout engine will: 1) mark the route as degraded and serve from the pinned fallback model variant, 2) surface an actionable remediation (apply synchronizer mapping OR unpin the new bundle), and 3) create a postmortem ticket with push-button repro steps for model owners.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full tokenizer normalization at bundle build (costly, slow) vs. lightweight probe + shim (faster onboarding, lower infra cost) — chosen shim approach to keep onboarding velocity.
- Aggressive automatic correction vs. human-in-the-loop for ambiguous cases — conservative policy: automated fixes only when mapping confidence >= 0.98, otherwise require manual approval.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for synchronizer divergence computation and mapping generator (coverage target 95%).
- Integration tests that spin up a small runtime with KV-cache enabled, run representative prompts, and assert cache hit parity and structured output stability.
- Canary rollout in staging: route 5% traffic through shimmed-onboard flow and run a battery of telemetry and correctness checks for 48 hours.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge synchronizer behind feature flag (ENG-658901/sync-ff).
2) Run onboarding pipeline on 20 recent bundles in staging; evaluate divergence vectors and mapping efficacy.
3) Enable shim for controlled customers/internal routes and monitor dashboards for 72 hours.
4) Remove feature flag and publish mapping artifacts to the model catalog as part of onboarding metadata.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Synchronizer+Design+Doc
- Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=7312345
- Initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1489
- Canary results dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/OnboardTokenSync/canary-2026-02

Notes:

- Inform Solutions and SRE about the runbook so they can onboard customers with pinned bundles that require manual mapping.
